officialTitle: Perioperative Nivolumab in Resectable Lung Cancer
clinicalQuestion: Does perioperative nivolumab (neoadjuvant with chemotherapy plus one year adjuvant) improve EFS over neoadjuvant chemotherapy in resectable stage IIA–IIIB NSCLC?

pico.population: Adults with resectable stage IIA to IIIB NSCLC
pico.intervention: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus chemotherapy every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, surgery, then adjuvant nivolumab every 4 weeks for 1 year (as sourced in arm dosing)
pico.comparator: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus placebo, surgery, then adjuvant placebo
pico.outcomes: Primary: EFS. Secondary: pCR, MPR, OS, safety

arms.label: Perioperative nivolumab
arms.regimen: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus chemotherapy, surgery, adjuvant nivolumab
arms.dosing: Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus chemotherapy every 3 weeks for 4 cycles; adjuvant nivolumab every 4 weeks for 1 year
arms.doseSourceQuote: neoadjuvant nivolumab plus chemotherapy or neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus placebo every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, followed by surgery and adjuvant nivolumab or placebo every 4 weeks for 1 year

arms.label: Placebo
arms.regimen: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus placebo, surgery, adjuvant placebo

publications.title: Perioperative Nivolumab in Resectable Lung Cancer.
publications.label: Prespecified interim analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: At this prespecified interim analysis (median follow-up, 25.4 months), the percentage of patients with 18-month event-free survival was 70.2% in the nivolumab group and 50.0% in the chemotherapy group (hazard ratio for disease progression or recurrence, abandoned surgery, or death, 0.58; 97.36% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.81; P<0.001).
A pathological complete response occurred in 25.3% of the patients in the nivolumab group and in 4.7% of those in the chemotherapy group (odds ratio, 6.64; 95% CI, 3.40 to 12.97)
a major pathological response occurred in 35.4% and 12.1%, respectively (odds ratio, 4.01; 95% CI, 2.48 to 6.49)

safety.sourceQuote: Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 32.5% of the patients in the nivolumab group and in 25.2% of those in the chemotherapy group.

strengths: EFS and pathological endpoints by blinded independent review
limitations: Cannot isolate contribution of the adjuvant phase versus neoadjuvant-only nivolumab (CheckMate 816)
Sample size not reported in the abstract

clinicalImplications.text: Supports perioperative nivolumab as an option for resectable stage IIA–IIIB NSCLC; whether adjuvant nivolumab adds benefit beyond neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy alone remains unresolved by randomised data.

tumourBoardPearl.text: CheckMate 77T adds a year of adjuvant nivolumab to the CheckMate 816 approach — the open question is who needs the adjuvant phase.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 38749033. Sample size not printed in the abstract and therefore omitted.
